input.summary:
parts/shell-b.mjs (plots 4-7 shells) now builds clean: the two off-palette shape variants are swapped for palette blocks (church lintel calcite_stairs x4 to quartz_stairs; side cornice calcite_slab x18 to quartz_slab). No REFUSED writes were reported for this part, so none were touched.
./make.sh rebuilds build.nbt with "part shells plots 4-7: 1142 placed" and no OFF-PALETTE or REFUSED line.
left: Not in my scope, flagged for the P5 stairs part: 'flight: the landing at 86,7,9 has no headroom' (owner flight x86 z14->10). The landing cell sits on the front wall line z9, which the shell skin fills, so the flight's top end needs a fix in the stairs part or in the plan's owner flight coordinates.

waste.what: Worked out which palette block replaces calcite_stairs and calcite_slab by reading palette.json's role lists by hand, then re-ran make.sh and grepped the output to confirm.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and one palette read; the fix itself was 3 edits
waste.tool: `mcd blocks --check calcite_stairs,calcite_slab` gives near names (it would have suggested quartz_*), and a palette check that prints a suggested swap per off-palette id would make the OFF-PALETTE line actionable without a lookup.

waste.what: make.sh's OFF-PALETTE line lists counts only, so the cell coordinates of the 22 off-palette blocks were not reported and had to be found by reading the source.
waste.cost: one read of shell-b.mjs; the blocks had to be matched to the lintel loop and the cornice loop by hand
waste.tool: parts-report.json (written by runParts) should list each off-palette block with its x,y,z so the owning part can jump straight to it.
